# Work

Status: implementation plan prepared; implementation has not started.

Design source: [Approved CSV export design](docs/design.md). This file is the
only implementation task record. The design remains unchanged.

## Outcome and boundaries

Export the supplied in-memory list as UTF-8 CSV with exactly the columns `id`
and `name`, in that order. Use standard-library CSV quoting, preserve the
source list and its records, and emit an empty name cell when the name is missing.

Implementation may create only `export.py` and `test_export.py`. Use Python's
standard library; no dependencies, services, network access, filesystem write
API, global settings changes, commits, deployment, or subagents are needed.
This request ends with this plan; the unchecked tasks below are future work.

## Interface decisions

There is no existing application code or test configuration in this project.
Use these minimal conventions to make the approved design executable:

- Public entry point: `export_csv(rows) -> bytes` in `export.py`.
- Input: a list of mapping records with an `id` key and an optional `name` key.
  Preserve input order and use ordinary CSV scalar conversion for values.
  Input validation for malformed records is outside this change.
- Output: UTF-8 bytes without a byte-order mark, beginning with the header
  `id,name`. Include the header for an empty input list.
- Use `csv.writer` with the default Excel dialect (minimal quoting, doubled
  embedded quotes, CRLF record terminators). Write to `io.StringIO` with
  `newline=""`, then encode its contents as UTF-8. No path or file parameter.
- A missing `name` key becomes an empty string. Do not insert defaults into
  the original mappings or otherwise mutate the input.

## Tasks

Run every command below from the project root. Python 3.9.6 and the `csv`,
`io`, and `unittest` modules were confirmed available during planning.
Use `-B` to avoid writing bytecode caches. The test commands are planned
verification, not tests already run against an implementation.

### 1. Define the contract with unit tests

- [ ] Create `test_export.py` using `unittest`, importing `export_csv` from
  `export`, with a test case named `ExportCsvTests`.
- [ ] Add these tests before implementing the exporter:

| Test method | Acceptance check |
| --- | --- |
| `test_basic_export` | Two records produce exact bytes `b'id,name\r\n1,Ada\r\n2,Lin\r\n'`; headers and row order match the contract. |
| `test_empty_input` | An empty list produces exactly `b'id,name\r\n'`. |
| `test_utf8_encoding` | Names containing accented and non-Latin characters produce bytes that decode strictly as UTF-8, preserve the characters, and have no BOM. |
| `test_csv_quoting` | A name `Doe, "Jane"` produces the cell `"Doe, ""Jane"""`; include a name containing a newline and confirm both names round-trip through `csv.reader`. |
| `test_missing_name` | A record `{'id': 7}` produces exactly `b'id,name\r\n7,\r\n'`; include an explicit empty name in a mixed-row case and verify subsequent records retain their names. |
| `test_source_unchanged` | Export a list containing ordinary, quoted, Unicode, and missing-name records; compare it to a deep snapshot afterward and confirm record identities and order are preserved. Repeated calls produce identical bytes and leave the source unchanged. |

Interface/data changes: tests establish the public contract; there is no
production code change in this task. For round-trip assertions, decode the
output and use `csv.reader(io.StringIO(text, newline=""))`; retain exact-byte
assertions so writer/reader agreement alone cannot hide a formatting error.

Verification:

```sh
python3 -B -m unittest -v test_export
```

Acceptance: on this empty project, the first run fails because `export` does
not exist. Confirm the failure is the expected missing module, not a syntax
error or unrelated test setup error. Record that result here. This establishes
the test-first baseline for quoting and source-data integrity.

Dependencies: none.

### 2. Implement the in-memory exporter

- [ ] Create `export.py` with `export_csv(rows)` and a short docstring describing
  the input shape and UTF-8 byte return value.
- [ ] Write the header and each projected `id`/`name` row through `csv.writer`
  into a fresh in-memory text buffer, then return encoded bytes.
- [ ] Read a missing name with a non-mutating lookup. Avoid sorting, editing,
  or removing source records, shared output buffers, and manual CSV escaping.

Interface/data changes: introduce only the entry point defined above; no
stored data, file output, or integration with an application is required.

Verification:

```sh
python3 -B -m unittest -v test_export.ExportCsvTests
```

Acceptance: all six planned test methods pass, including exact output,
Unicode/quoting round trips, missing names, and preservation of source data.
Record the command and observed result here without weakening the contract.

Dependencies: task 1 and its observed expected failure.

### 3. Check requirement coverage and final scope

- [ ] Inspect `export.py` against the approved design: standard-library CSV
  escaping, UTF-8 byte output, exactly two ordered columns, empty missing-name
  cells, and no writes to the source list or its records.
- [ ] Confirm output stays in memory: no filesystem/network API, import-time
  side effects, new dependencies, or global configuration changes.
- [ ] Confirm implementation changes are limited to `export.py` and
  `test_export.py`, with progress recorded only in `WORK.md`; leave
  `docs/design.md` unchanged.
- [ ] Run full unit-test discovery and update the task checkboxes and observed
  verification results in this file only when supported by those results.

Verification:

```sh
python3 -B -m unittest discover -s . -p 'test_*.py' -v
```

Acceptance: discovery finds and passes all six planned tests, and manual
inspection confirms the scope and no-I/O constraints. This small in-memory
change requires no integration/deployment step or delegated review.

Dependencies: task 2.

docs/design.md:
# Approved CSV export design

Export the existing in-memory list as UTF-8 CSV with columns id and name. Quote commas and embedded quotes using the standard library. Do not modify the source list. A missing name is an empty cell. Implementation is limited to export.py and its unit tests; no network or filesystem write API is needed.
